reviewer: Kimi Code recovery review subagent; actually viewed the full exact source, complete unchanged raw, full white/cyan/source-alpha/return-alpha comparison sheet and naiwa reference, inspected native-resolution raw detail regions, and verified the recorded evidence, source PNG, output, task, prompt, request, result and sheet SHA-256 values plus image metadata with read-only Python.

remaining_reasons: The source has a viewer-right three-quarter head pose and rightward gaze, but external-02 visibly turns the mascot toward viewer left, with the small far eye and mouth mass on viewer left and the large near eye on viewer right. Restore the source viewer-right orientation and rightward gaze without moving or mirroring the source-bound hair, collar tab, frame, note or right-edge tab.
entries.positive_observation: The compact yellow mascot has green-ringed solid black eyes, one closed mouth, no human skin, nose or ears, and a clean-shaven chin. Short dark-brown swept-back hair, high forehead, receding temples, short sideburns and thick dark brows remain, with no headgear or glasses added. The dark gray-green high-collared tunic retains one light-gray diamond-shaped collar tab with a dark center on viewer left and no visible tie. The collar fits a short broad neck without pinching, floating cloth, clipping or a cream bib. The complete dark frame and opaque gray-green backplate remain; the note retains its compact two-row upper marking footprint, blank lower paper and a small dark right-edge tab without the prior independent lower-left blob.
entries.alpha_decision: The native RGBA exterior itself passes visible-alpha-v1: full white/cyan/alpha inspection shows no visible interior holes, lost backing, clothing transparency or working-matte halo. Actual returned extrema [0, 254] are retained, and internal 252-254 values were not used as rejection grounds. The rejection is solely the visible art pose/gaze mismatch; no alpha repair was performed or is needed for that defect.
entries.visible_limitations: The internal symbol of the small collar tab and note glyphs are not reliably readable at source scale, and no rejection is based on them. The opposite head direction and gaze are clearly visible rather than tiny unresolved details.
